THE FINDINGS

Broaden exposure. Keep evidence visible.

There are missed exploration opportunities.

Market research for Valentina, exercise physiology for Darius, care-role alternatives for Jordan and property representation for Valentina deserve clearer exposure. None is an automatic Top promotion.

Other absences make sense as unresolved cases: cooking is not customer service; tutoring is not family-service casework; listening is not professional counseling.

Visibility and interest are different.

The model chart shows three comparison invitations. Exercise physiology is rank 17 for Darius, nursing assistant rank 7 for Jordan, and real estate rank 8 for Valentina in the full comparison set.

The Other list also caps six before pending offers are removed. That can hide related alternatives. Changing visibility would not confirm their interest fit.

Doctor, lawyer and engineer are already present.

The current public replay contains the offers below. The expanded inventory now includes separate physician specialties and engineering domains. Top eligibility depends on supported role-specific interests.

Inspect current counts ↓

The inventory is now much wider.

Systematic O*NET/BLS selection supplies 404 profiles: 276 college and 128 graduate/professional. 27 lack complete interest vectors and remain browse-only.

Degree or prestige does not raise interest scores. Experienced destinations are labeled and omitted by default. Source gaps do not become invented pay or aptitude.

HOW ESTABLISHED SERVICES DO IT

Discover a pattern before naming a job.

Established tools still ask about activities. Some also include job titles. What matters is the wider pattern, the construct being measured, the evidence behind the linkage and the opportunity to learn before deciding.

O*NET / My Next MoveActivity preferences: six RIASEC interests

Sum official activity preferences into six scores; compare the whole profile with occupational interests using documented correlation and presentation rules. Preparation levels are explored separately.

THE REVISED DESIGN

Discover → connect → learn → reflect.

  1. Start with underlying interests.

    Keep the official activity inventory intact. Use varied subjects, problem types and contexts without showing career prestige or pay first. Narrow interests can refine broad themes; new editorial probes need their own evaluation.

  2. Keep strengths and aptitude separate.

    Report existing experience and confidence honestly. Do not turn self-ratings into measured ability. Performance-based aptitude needs an appropriate validated assessment and administration, not improvised puzzle scores.

  3. Retrieve across the full inventory.

    Compare the complete six-interest profile across all available occupational vectors before choosing one field. Expose missing evidence and alternatives; allow search and topic browsing even with an open or incomplete profile.

  4. Provide neutral career exposure.

    Show the problems, settings and varieties of work, including adjacent roles. Do not make professional jargon, existing skills, a family connection or prior job access prerequisites to interest.

  5. Ask for an informed reaction.

    Record what became more interesting, what became less appealing and what remains unknown. Use specific work questions to resolve a remaining distinction after learning, not to hide a profession before discovery.

  6. Plan feasibility separately.

    Compare training, admission, supports, licensing, costs and realistic first paid stages. Salary cannot establish interest. A broader inventory improves opportunity coverage without guaranteeing a confirmed match.

Concrete later-stage branches: medicine, law, engineering, research and decision science

Physician, beginning with family medicine

Interest in disease mechanisms plus patient-facing diagnosis, or explicit medical exploration; generic helping alone is insufficient.

  • defining: Would you enjoy learning to compare a patient’s symptoms, health history and test results to work out what may be causing an illness?
  • distinct defining: Would you enjoy learning to choose a medical treatment with a patient and check over time whether it is helping?
  • adjacent-role contrast: Which work would you like to investigate further: diagnosing and treating an individual patient; studying disease in a research project; tracking illness across a community; or supporting daily patient care? Choose any, or unsure.
  • clarification: Imagine two illnesses could explain the same symptoms. Would comparing the evidence and explaining why one diagnosis fits better hold your interest?
  • route, separate: After learning about this work, would you like to compare medical school and residency with other health-care preparation routes?

Patient diagnosis+treatment opens physician/PA/NP work comparisons with neutral scope/role descriptions; research opens medical scientist; community patterns opens epidemiology. Definite dislike of direct clinical work should not imply dislike of medical science. No automatic physician promotion from two generic helping answers.

O*NET29-1215.00 Family Medicine Physicians ↗

Lawyer

Interest in rights/rules plus using evidence or careful language to advise/represent others. Being argumentative, sociable or interested in fairness alone is insufficient.

  • defining: Would you enjoy learning to read laws and earlier legal decisions to explain how they apply to someone’s situation?
  • distinct defining: Would you enjoy learning to build a well-supported legal recommendation after comparing facts and opposing arguments?
  • role variants: Which legal activities would you like to try learning: advising a client; drafting a contract; negotiating a dispute; presenting an argument in court; or organizing evidence for a legal team? Choose any, or unsure.
  • clarification: If a case has a sympathetic person but mixed evidence, would you want to investigate the facts and explain the limits of their legal position?
  • context, separate: How do you feel about work that involves substantial reading, precise writing and deadlines?

Core legal analysis+advice can support law exploration even if courtroom performance is unattractive; legal-team evidence work opens paralegal; general policy/justice interest opens public policy/social research. Do not make criminal defense, litigation or enjoying public speaking mandatory for all lawyers.

O*NET23-1011.00 Lawyers ↗

Engineering, then domain-specific roles

Interest in designing/test-improving systems under real constraints, or explicit domain exploration; liking mathematics or assembling things alone is insufficient.

  • domain discovery: Which problems would you like to learn to design solutions for: machines and motion; electricity and electronics; buildings and water systems; materials and chemical processes; aircraft and spacecraft; computer hardware; medical devices; or production systems? Choose any, or unsure.
  • defining: Would you enjoy learning to compare design options using calculations and tests before deciding which solution is likely to work?
  • distinct defining: Would you enjoy revising a design when tests show a weakness, while balancing safety, cost and how people will use it?
  • adjacent-role contrast: Would you rather explore designing a new system, building/installing it, maintaining and repairing it, or investigating the science behind it? Choose any, or unsure.
  • domain-specific differentiator: For medical devices: would designing equipment used to diagnose or treat health conditions interest you, even when much of the work is testing and documenting rather than caring directly for patients?

Domain selection opens matching engineer/technician/scientist/trade activities. Preserve overlap without treating interest in generic gadgets as biomedical interest. Environmental/chemical/computer/aerospace branches require their own sourced questions and route/pay data before live matching.

O*NET17-2141.00 Mechanical Engineers ↗ · O*NET Content Model ↗

Medical scientist

Interest in biology/disease and experimental investigation; can emerge from science or health, including dislike of patient care.

  • defining: Would you enjoy learning to design a study that tests a possible explanation for how a disease develops or how a treatment works?
  • distinct defining: Would you enjoy learning to analyze biological samples or research results and explain what they do and do not show?
  • adjacent-role contrast: Would you prefer to investigate disease in a research study, diagnose individual patients, or study health patterns in whole communities? Choose any, or unsure.
  • context, separate: Would repeating a careful procedure and checking unexpected results appeal to you, or would you want to learn more about that routine first?

Research/design interest opens medical scientist; reliable-lab-procedure interest may also open biological technician or clinical laboratory scientist; patient diagnosis routes toward clinical roles; population patterns routes toward epidemiology. Do not require intent to practice medicine.

O*NET19-1042.00 Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists ↗

Operations research analyst

Interest in quantitative decision-making under constraints; can connect data, logistics, public-service or engineering interests.

  • defining: Would you enjoy learning to build a mathematical model that compares ways to use limited staff, time or resources?
  • distinct defining: Would you enjoy testing how a recommended plan changes when demand, costs or assumptions change?
  • adjacent-role contrast: Would you like to explore optimizing a decision with a model, finding patterns in data, coordinating an agreed project, or designing physical equipment? Choose any, or unsure.
  • context, separate: Would explaining a model’s assumptions and limitations to people making a decision interest you?

Optimization under constraints opens operations research; pattern-finding opens data science/statistics; coordination opens project/logistics roles. Spreadsheet familiarity or enjoyment of gaming strategy alone does not establish the profession.

O*NET15-2031.00 Operations Research Analysts ↗

Medicine and law need varieties, not duplicate prestige labels

17-2061 · O*NET 17-2061.00 · College emphasis

Interests to distinguish: Design and test the physical components of computing systems

A degree-qualified entry role is distinct from senior, lead, manager, independent consultant or licensed sign-off responsibility; additional requirements vary by employer and jurisdiction.

Gaming, assembling a PC, and troubleshooting can open exploration but do not by themselves establish new-hardware design interest.

Use these drafts after broad discovery and neutral career exposure. They do not measure aptitude and are not a validated assessment bank.

Nearby-role comparison: Would you rather design new computer parts, write applications, help people fix existing computers, or explore more than one?

Allow several interests, neither or unsure. Do not treat unfamiliarity as dislike.

Interests to distinguish: Adult learning · Instruction design · Facilitation and evaluation

BLS less than five years related work experience; experience may come from teaching, HR or a field being taught; Certification voluntary/employer-specific; not public-school teacher licensure

Adds adult learning and practical workplace instruction; teaching interests need not imply classroom school teaching.

Use these drafts after broad discovery and neutral career exposure. They do not measure aptitude and are not a validated assessment bank.

  1. Would you like to learn to find out what employees need to learn and design a useful practice activity or short course?
  2. Would you like to learn to lead workplace training and improve it after checking whether employees can use the new skill?

Nearby-role comparison: Which would you rather learn: help adults learn skills they use at work, or teach school-age students an academic curriculum?

Allow several interests, neither or unsure. Do not treat unfamiliarity as dislike.

EVIDENCE & LIMITS

Measure quality, not filled slots.

The expanded inventory is live for browsing and interest connections in the student guide and every model preview. It is available before a field choice. Release0.47 activates313 added professions for Top matching after three distinct supported reflections and strong complete-profile alignment. The27 residual categories remain browse-only. Earlier Top lists and frozen original responses remain preserved. Compare the current rerun with0.46 →

Next evaluation should use biographies and independently authored underlying-interest answers frozen before outcomes. Review relevance, missed good alternatives and unsupported promotions separately. Record eligible, visible, opened, learned-about and confirmed stages, including the strongest missing distinction.

  • Audit exact SOCs and broader education mappings; never duplicate specialties to inflate coverage.
  • Review title/order effects and understanding before and after neutral previews. Do not claim title masking alone removes bias.
  • Check narrower-interest coverage, reading accessibility, unfamiliar work and negative evidence. Use multiple realistic activities without counting paraphrases as independent support.
  • Use independent counselor review and prospective student usability/outcome studies. Frozen fictional models establish software behavior, not student matching validity.
  • Source training, licensing, local pay, prior experience and first paid stage before adding a career to lifestyle planning. Missing data stays unknown.
  • No target quota for degree professions, matches per student or budget coverage. A genuine no-match result can be appropriate.
Observed code gates to evaluate next

careerComparisonOptions

No comparison invitations for incomplete, flat or near-flat profiles. Entry requires eligible whole-profile fit plus an opportunity or focused-field like; alternate opportunity route requiresr>=.2andtaskEvidence>=3. All-connected-field conflict and role/route conflict also suppress invitations.

Risk: Plausible narrow interests can remain unasked when a broad profile is weak or field questions do not represent them. This is a code-path risk, not proof that this caused any specific zero count.

Proposed check: Allow an explicitly labeled student-selected discovery path from search or a domain probe even with incomplete/flat profiles. Keep Top evidence standards separate and explain why results are provisional.

careerComparisonsPanel

First3invitations are immediately visible; remaining options are inside More professions to compare.

Risk: Visibility and eligible-candidate availability differ. A zero in displayed match counts can reflect ordering/caps rather than career ineligibility.

Proposed check: Record eligible/invited/visible/started/completed separately; expose domain-diverse exploration and user search.

journeyFieldConnection / broadSuggestions

Field support uses mean correlation of3leading catalog occupations, threshold.608, plus focused-field confirmation and fewer than2concerns. Suggested fields are capped3.

Risk: The field score depends on current catalog composition; adding careers can change field exposure before any new student answer.

Proposed check: Freeze/version field vectors or explicitly audit expansion effects on old fields. Offer all fields through exploration navigation.

professionSuggestions

Direct support requires3nonroute question groups and2derived domains plus whole-profile fit or a6group repeated-task alternative. The alternative further needs3refinement groups and4focused groups; counting depends on selected options.

Risk: Repeated variants of the same activity can look like independent evidence, while a profession omitted from mapped options cannot gather enough evidence.

Proposed check: Represent activity/domain/outcome evidence explicitly. Count semantically distinct constructs, not question IDs alone; give each new profession balanced positive, adjacent and contradiction probes.

taskEvidenceDomain / careerCheckSpec

Evidence domain is inferred from question ID substrings. One family with most matching nonroute questions is selected;4questions chosen for specificity/domain coverage.

Risk: Naming conventions can create artificial independence. Cross-field professions are reduced to one family; more catalog entries can increase repeated shared options without useful differentiation.

Proposed check: Add explicit domain/construct/role-family/question-purpose metadata and source mappings. Reuse relevant cross-field responses and branch to the missing differentiator.

health-role-work / health-role-observe / health-role-learning

Clinical-role checks distinguish7medical/dental roles. Physician, NP and PA share many broad items, then role names and preparation routes separate them. health focusedRoles excludes other roles when a focused role has been selected.

Risk: A novice can understand symptom investigation yet not know PA/NP/physician responsibilities or route terminology. More specifically, roleFocusElsewhere applies to every health-family occupation once any focused clinical role is selected, so a clinical choice can exclude nonclinical health ideas such as epidemiology in that family. This is an actual gate; its contribution to observed model counts still needs a controlled replay.

Proposed check: Provide neutral role explanations and work scenarios before named-role choices; support multiple interests. Keep actual prescribing scope, training and licensure accurate and separate from interest.

building questions

Mechanical, electrical and biomedical engineering share many identical options; biomedical is linked to generic devices/circuits before its2defining medical-device questions. Catalog contains5engineering occupations.

Risk: Question count overstates breadth; repeated generic device evidence cannot decide a medical-device interest or reveal omitted chemical/environmental/computer/aerospace areas.

Proposed check: Probe design object and problem domain before specialization; map a given domain to engineer, technician, researcher and trade alternatives with differentiated work activities.

coreWorkStatus

Current0.44requires2defining Yes responses. Direct responses support confirmation; inferred responses support only high/medium confidence. ExplicitNo declines; unsure/unfamiliar stays pending.

Risk: Improved content avoids the former unfamiliar-tools gate, but2Yes is an editorial rule, not a validated standard. Leading or compound prompts can still inflate endorsement.

Proposed check: Keep provenance and unresolvedness visible; test single-concept wording, contradictions and alternate second probes. Never treat inferred answers as real student choices.

invitation ordering

Among similar relevance candidates, education preference and lifestyle coverage affect invitation ordering. A relevant degree option is inserted if willing/open to college or graduate study and the initial3have none.

Risk: This helps exposure but cannot establish suitability. Pay and education routing can change which questions are answered before outcomes are calculated.

Proposed check: Measure exposure stratified by route and interest strength. Keep salary, prestige, education preference and affordability outside interest evidence.

These are implementation risks, not a claim that each caused a particular model outcome. The12-profile trace above identifies the observed cases.
